Chapter One

The morning train crossed the valley while the last fog lifted from the river. Elena opened her notebook and wrote one clear sentence: a small tool should do one useful job well. She read the line twice, closed the cover, and watched the hills turn gold.

At the next station, a family stepped aboard with a bright red suitcase. The youngest child counted every bridge aloud. Each number arrived with such confidence that the other passengers began to smile. By the seventh bridge, even the conductor was listening.

When the train reached the coast, the air smelled of salt and pine. Elena carried her bag to a quiet bench above the harbor. Boats moved below like white commas on a blue page. She opened the notebook again and added a second line: good work should feel calm, direct, and complete.
